generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The version id `8_656_00_0` is valid Java (equals 8 656 000) but the underscore grouping is unconventional compared to the typical three-digit grouping (e.g. `8_656_000`). This is a minor readability nit, but worth aligning with the project's existing convention for transport version ids to avoid confusion when scanning the list.

review_comment: I think it might be more clear here to put `startSize2` as the produced expected value, since the ingested and produced should be the same for failure and drop.

This comment made me aware that there might be a bug around here because I'm not sure these values are actually supposed to be equal, I think it just turns out that way because the mock processors aren't modifying the data so there's no increase in bytes.

But I dug into this a little bit more and realized I misremembered this part of the test as [this test](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/12b31e79caa67fd717ffa49166eff54e179acca9/server/src/test/java/org/elasticsearch/ingest/IngestServiceTests.java#L181) when we brought up testing a failure
And I think parts of this test don't behave the way I thought it did (in the 3rd test the byte stats values for `_id1` hasn't increased, and in the 4th with the failure `startSize1` is equal to `endSize1`), so I'm going to dig into this a bit more

Figured out what was wrong - when the stats of a pipeline gets updated via another pipeline's stats it wasn't updating the `IngestPipelineMetric` stats, so I fixed that and changed some of the tests as necessary

Good catch on figuring out what was going on here, and fixing the `IngestPipelineMetric.add` method.

As an aside, I was at first very confused about why the `endSize1` was increasing despite the failure. Also why the `_id1` pipeline has a `failed` count of 0 in the ` assertPipelineStats` call above. I had missed that the failure-mock has an `on_failure` processor defined. When there is an on_failure processor, the resulting document does get sent to the index, so that explains why it is in the bytesProduced stat. (You may have been aware of all this already).
Yeah that was part of what led me to investigating that section, I didn't realize at first that `endSize1` was increasing there
